questions.question: Akhil bought 13 kg of apples for Rs. 2,400. He sold them at a profit equal to the selling price of 7 kg of apples. Find the selling price of apples per kg.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost price (CP) of 13 kg apples = Rs. 2400

Profit = Selling Price (SP) of 7 kg apples

**Concept:**

The formula to find the Selling Price (SP) is SP = CP + Profit.

**Solution:**

Let SP of 1 kg apple be x.

⇒ SP of 13 kg apples = 13x.

⇒ Profit = SP of 7 kg apples = 7x.

According to the problem, SP = CP + Profit.

⇒ 13x = 2400 + 7x.

⇒ 13x - 7x = 2400.

⇒ 6x = 2400.

⇒ x = 2400/6.

⇒ x = Rs. 400.

**Therefore, the selling price of apples per kg is Rs. 400.**

questions.question: D alone can do a work in 20 days and E alone can do the same work in 25 days. If they work on it together for 8 days, then the fraction of the work that left is:

questions.question: Find the fourth proportion to 8, 14 and 24.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Three numbers: 8, 14, 24

**Concept:** In the fourth proportion, if a:b = c:d, then d is the fourth proportion to a, b, c.

**Solution:**

⇒ a/b = c/d

⇒ 8/14 = 24/d

⇒ d = (24 × 14)/8

⇒ d = 42.

**Therefore, the fourth proportion to 8, 14, and 24 is 42.**

questions.question: Sajid drove for 6 hours at a rate of 60 km/hr and for 4 hours at 50 km/hr. What was his average speed for the whole Journey?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Sajid drives for 6 hours at 60 km/hr

Sajid drives for 4 hours at 50 km/hr

**Concept:** Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Solution:**

⇒ Total distance covered = (6 hours × 60 km/hr) + (4 hours × 50 km/hr) = 360 km + 200 km = 560 km

⇒ Total time = 6 hours + 4 hours = 10 hours

⇒ Average speed = 560 km / 10 hours = 56 km/hr

**Therefore, Sajid's average speed for the whole journey is 56 km/hr.**

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is six times of its breadth and the height of cuboid is four times of its breadth. If the breadth of the cuboid is 3 cm, then what is the total surface area of cuboid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given breadth (b) = 3 cm.

Length (l) = 6 × 3 = 18 cm, Height (h) = 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (18 × 3 + 3 × 12 + 12 × 18)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (54 + 36 + 216) = 2 × 306 = 612 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 612 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Breadth of the cuboid (b) = 3 cm

Length of the cuboid (l) = 6 × b = 6 × 3 = 18 cm

Height of the cuboid (h) = 4 × b = 4 × 3 = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50fb8bb272489b952705a05d3b8f9cb9e7b4534bcc969a25e01d04e7217d07b.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of base (l × b) = 18 × 3 = 54 cm²

⇒ Area of side (b × h) = 3 × 12 = 36 cm²

⇒ Area of front (h × l) = 12 × 18 = 216 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (54 + 36 + 216)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 306

⇒ Total Surface Area = 612 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 612 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The formula for the volume is V = l × b × h, representing the total 3D space occupied by the object.

Lateral Surface Area of a Cuboid

The lateral surface area excludes the top and bottom faces. The formula is LSA = 2h(l + b).

Longest Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can fit inside the cuboid is calculated using d = √(l² + b² + h²).

Special Case: Cube

When length, breadth, and height are all equal (l = b = h = a), the cuboid becomes a cube. Its Total Surface Area is 6a².

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 17 km/hr and the speed of a stream is 11 km/hr. Find the difference between the upstream speed and the downstream speed of the boat.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **difference** between **downstream speed** and **upstream speed** is always equal to **twice the speed of the stream**.

Difference = 2 × **Stream Speed**

⇒ Difference = 2 × 11 km/hr

⇒ Difference = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in **still water** (u) = 17 km/hr

Speed of the **stream** (v) = 11 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eebd3eb967a14c858ed8b0fc70780474253f60a54b7f07be898a524dd783ee97.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (D) = u + v

Upstream Speed (U) = u − v

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 17 + 11 = 28 km/hr

⇒ Upstream speed = 17 − 11 = 6 km/hr

⇒ Required Difference = Downstream speed − Upstream speed

⇒ Difference = 28 − 6 = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

When going downstream, the stream assists the boat; when going upstream, the stream opposes the boat.</p

questions.question: The average of numbers A and B is 16. The average of numbers B and C is 40. What is the difference between C and A?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in averages of (B, C) and (A, B) = 40 − 16 = 24.

Since both sets consist of 2 numbers and B is common, the difference between the unique numbers is double the difference of their averages.

Difference between C and A = 2 × 24 = 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of A and B = 16

Average of B and C = 40

**Formula Used:**

Sum of numbers = Average × Number of items

 
 A + B = 32
 
 B + C = 80
 
• 
 
• 
 

 Difference (C − A) = 80 − 32 = 48
 Sum Comparison

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average of A and B = (A + B) ÷ 2 = 16

⇒ A + B = 16 × 2 = 32 → (Eq. 1)

⇒ Average of B and C = (B + C) ÷ 2 = 40

⇒ B + C = 40 × 2 = 80 → (Eq. 2)

Subtracting (Eq. 1) from (Eq. 2):

⇒ (B + C) − (A + B) = 80 − 32

⇒ B + C − A − B = 48

⇒ C − A = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Difference Property

If Average(x, y) = M and Average(y, z) = N, then the difference (z − x) = 2 × (N − M).

Weighted Average

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and x is the value/average.</p

questions.question:
Cash reserve ratio is a ________ tool to control money supply.

I. Qualitative

II. Quantitative
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Monetary policy tools are of two types - 

 
• Quantitative Monetary policy tools
 
• Qualitative Monetary policy tools

 

Quantitative instruments influence the money volume and credit supply in the system.

The quantitative instruments are Open Market Operations, Liquidity Adjustment Facility (Repo and Reverse Repo), Marginal Standing Facility, SLR, CRR, Bank Rate, etc.

Open Market Operations:

__
 
• Open market operations (OMO) refers to the buying and selling of government securities in the open market in order to expand or contract the amount of money in the banking system, facilitated by the Federal Reserve.
 
• Open Market Operations are carried out in Gilt Edged Market.

Cash Reserve Ratio:

 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as balances with the RBI.
 
• The objective of CRR is to keep inflation under control.
 
• During high inflation in the economy, the central bank raises the CRR to lower the bank’s loanable funds.

Bank Rate: 

 
• The RBI can influence money supply by changing the rate at which it gives loans to the commercial banks. This rate is called the Bank Rate in India.
 
• By increasing the bank rate, loans taken by commercial banks become more expensive; this reduces the reserves held by the commercial bank and hence decreases the money supply. A fall in the bank rate can increase the money supply.

Margin Requirments:

 
• Margin requirement refers to the difference between the current value of the security offered for loan (called collateral) and the value of loan granted.
 
• It is a qualitative method of credit control adopted by the central bank in order to stabilize the economy from inflation or deflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Qualitative Monetary tools used in monetary policy regulation are as follows:

 
• Fixing Margin Requirements: The margin refers to the “proportion of the loan amount which is not financed by the bank”. Or in other words, it is that part of a loan which a borrower has to raise in order to get finance for his purpose. A change in a margin implies a change in the loan size.
 
• Consumer Credit Regulation: Under this method, the consumer credit supply is regulated through the hire-purchase and installment sale of consumer goods. This can help in checking the credit use and then inflation in a country.
 
• Publicity: This is yet another method of selective credit control. Through it, Central Bank (RBI) publishes various reports stating what is good and what is bad in the system. This published information can help commercial banks to direct credit supply in the desired sectors.
 
• Credit Rationing: Central Bank fixes the credit amount to be granted. Credit is rationed by limiting the amount available for each commercial bank. This method controls even bill re-discounting. For certain purposes, the upper limit of credit can be fixed and banks are told to stick to this limit. This can help in lowering banks' credit exposure to unwanted sectors.
 
• Moral Suasion: It implies to pressure exerted by the RBI on the Indian banking system without any strict action for compliance with the rules. It is a suggestion to banks. It helps in restraining credit during inflationary periods. Under moral suasion, central banks can issue directives, guidelines, and suggestions for commercial banks regarding reducing credit supply for speculative purposes.
 
• Control Through Directives: Under this method the central bank issue frequent directives to commercial banks. These directives guide commercial banks in framing their lending policy. Through a directive, the central bank can influence credit structures, the supply of credit to certain limits for a specific purpose. The RBI issues directives to commercial banks for not lending loans to the speculative sectors such as securities, etc beyond a certain limit.
 
• Direct Action: Under this method, the RBI can impose action against a bank. If certain banks are not adhering to the RBI’s directives, the RBI may refuse to re-discount their bills and securities.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Law of Inertia, **Newton's first law of motion, states that an object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
• The term **'inertia' refers to the resistance of an object to change its state of motion.**
 
• It can be thought of as a property of mass to resist change.
 
• If an object is at rest,** it will remain at rest unless an unbalanced force acts upon it.**
 
• If an object is in motion**, it will continue to move in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.**
 
• This law introduces the concept of a frame of reference.
 
• The descriptions of motion** depend on the observer, and different observers may observe different states of motion.**
 
• An important consequence of this law is the** idea of conservation of momentum.**
 
• If the net force on an object is zero,** its momentum (mass times velocity) remains constant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion include three fundamental principles:**
 
• **Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia):**
 
 
• **​**An object will remain at** rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law:**
 
 
• **​**The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the force applied.
 
• It is typically formulated as ***F=ma*, where F is the force applied, m is the mass of the object, and a is the acceleration produced.**
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law:**
 
 
• **​**For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It means that any force exerted on a **body will create a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the object which exerted the first force.**
